verses.text: I said in my heart, "Come now, I will test you with fun. Enjoy pleasure." But look, this also was meaningless.
I said about laughter, "It is foolish," and about fun, "What good does it do?"

I searched in my heart how to cheer myself with wine, while my heart still guided me with wisdom, and how to take hold of foolishness, until I could see what is good for people to do under heaven all the days of their lives.
I did great works. I built houses for myself. I planted vineyards for myself.
I made gardens and parks for myself, and I planted all kinds of fruit trees in them.
I made pools of water for myself, to water the forest where the trees were growing.
I bought male and female servants, and I had servants born in my house. I also owned great herds and flocks, more than anyone in Jerusalem before me.
I also gathered silver and gold for myself, and the treasures of kings and provinces. I got men and women singers, and the pleasures people delight in: musical instruments of every kind.
So I became great, and grew richer than anyone in Jerusalem before me. And my wisdom stayed with me.
I did not keep from my eyes anything they wanted. I did not hold back my heart from any joy, for my heart was glad because of all my work, and this was my reward for all my work.
Then I looked at all the things my hands had done, and at the work I had worked so hard to do. And look, everything was meaningless, like chasing the wind. Nothing was gained under the sun.
I turned to think about wisdom, madness, and foolishness. For what can the king who comes after me do? Only what has already been done long ago.
Then I saw that wisdom is better than foolishness, just as light is better than darkness.
The wise person has eyes in their head, but the fool walks in darkness. And yet I saw that the same end happens to them all.
Then I said in my heart, "What happens to the fool will happen to me too. So why was I so wise?" Then I said in my heart that this too is meaningless.
For the wise person, like the fool, will not be remembered forever. In the days to come, everyone will long be forgotten. Yes, the wise person must die just like the fool!
So I hated life, because the work done under the sun was painful to me. Everything is meaningless, like chasing the wind.
I hated all the hard work I had done under the sun, because I must leave it to the person who comes after me.
And who knows whether that person will be wise or foolish? Yet they will be in charge of all the work I have done with such effort and wisdom under the sun. This too is meaningless.
So my heart began to give up hope about all the hard work I had done under the sun.
For a person may work with wisdom, knowledge, and skill, and then have to leave everything they own to someone who never worked for it. This too is meaningless and a great evil.
For what do people get from all their hard work and from all the striving of their hearts under the sun?
All their days are full of pain, and their work is full of grief. Even at night their hearts do not rest. This too is meaningless.
There is nothing better for a person than to eat and drink and enjoy the good in their work. I saw that this also comes from the hand of God.
For who can eat or enjoy anything more than I can?

To the person who pleases him, God gives wisdom, knowledge, and joy. But to the sinner he gives the work of gathering and storing up, to give it to the one who pleases God. This too is meaningless, like chasing the wind.
